market_context: United States and Canada; practical, safety-first household guidance written natively for North American readers.
title: What Temperature Should You Set the AC to in Summer?

seo.title: What Temperature Should You Set the AC to in Summer?
seo.meta_description: There is no single ideal AC temperature. Use the highest comfortable setting and account for humidity, fans, occupancy, and schedule to reduce energy use.
seo.search_intent: Choose a summer air-conditioning setpoint that balances comfort, humidity, and energy use without presenting one number as universally correct.

excerpt: The “perfect” number changes with climate, humidity, clothing, activity, and household needs. For efficiency, the useful principle is keeping the home as warm as remains comfortable.
content_html:
There is no mandatory setpoint for every home. The U.S. Department of Energy recommends using the highest temperature that remains comfortable and adjusting settings when the home is unoccupied.

Start with comfort and humidity

A dry climate and a humid climate can feel very different at the same temperature. If the house is cool but clammy, the issue may be moisture removal rather than an excessively high setpoint.

Make small changes

Raise the setting a degree, wait, and evaluate. Gradual changes reveal the comfort threshold without creating unnecessary large recovery cycles.

Use fans where people are present

Air movement improves perceived comfort and can allow a slightly higher thermostat setting. Turn fans off in empty rooms.

Do not compensate for a hot house with an extremely low setting

Most air conditioners do not cool faster because you select a much lower temperature; they simply run longer trying to reach it.

If the system cannot reach a reasonable setpoint, diagnose the problem

A dirty filter, blocked outdoor unit, open doors, strong solar gain, or equipment fault can prevent normal performance. Lowering the thermostat further does not fix those causes.

The practical summer setting is the highest one that maintains acceptable comfort and humidity for the people in the home, with sensible adjustments when nobody is there.

faq.question: Is there one official ideal AC temperature?
faq.answer: No. Efficiency guidance provides strategies, while comfort depends on climate, humidity, and occupants.

faq.question: Will setting the thermostat to 60°F cool the house faster?
faq.answer: Usually no. It mainly makes the system run longer trying to reach a very low setpoint.

faq.question: Can a fan let me set the thermostat higher?
faq.answer: It can improve comfort for people in the room and may allow a slightly higher setting.
